The Splendid alfonsino Beryx splendens is a benthopelagic species supporting notable commercial fisheries across seamounts of the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. Spawning adults release small, buoyant eggs that are pelagic and subject to extensive dispersal by oceanic currents. The fertilised ovum measures approximately 1.1 mm in diameter, and the resulting yolk-sac larva emerges with an extremely small body mass, with wet weight at birth calculated at 0.0007 grams [Wwb = 0.0007 grams]. This minute starting size reflects a high fecundity strategy in which large numbers of tiny offspring are broadcast into a variable environment. Juvenile fish experience rapid somatic growth during their first few years, but attaining the ultimate total length of 70 centimeters [Li = 70 centimeters] requires many years of sustained feeding in productive waters. The species is known for its relatively slow growth rate and late maturation compared with many other commercially exploited teleosts.

Field surveys and otolith-based aging studies have provided robust estimates of the key size thresholds associated with reproductive development. The total length at puberty, marking the onset of gonadal recrudescence, has been determined to be 33.2 centimeters [Lp = 33.2 centimeters], a value consistent across several geographically distinct populations examined. Individuals below this threshold exhibit immature gonads and are not yet reproductively viable. Reaching this size typically coincides with an age of several years, reflecting the energetic demands of accumulating sufficient body reserves prior to vitellogenesis onset. The ultimate wet weight of maximally sized adults, by contrast, has been recorded at approximately 4000 grams [Wwi = approximately 4000 grams] from specimens approaching the asymptotic length. This considerable body mass, almost six thousand times the weight at birth, underscores the dramatic ontogenetic scaling of this deepwater species.

Under controlled laboratory conditions maintained at a stable temperature of 10 °C [T = 10 °C], researchers have quantified the maximum reproductive output of this species. Each spawning event results in the release of numerous eggs, and the daily reproduction rate during peak activity, representing the number of eggs produced per day across the full season, reaches approximately 1850 eggs per day [Ri = approximately 1850 eggs per day], with this rate sustained over several consecutive weeks. This elevated fecundity is characteristic of pelagic spawners that rely on high larval numbers to offset the intense mortality experienced during the early planktonic phase. The reproductive season is protracted, and gravid individuals have been captured throughout much of the year in warmer waters, although spawning intensity may vary with local oceanographic conditions and prey availability.

The lifespan of the Splendid alfonsino has been investigated through otolith annulus counts and mark-recapture data from long-term tagging programs. At the same thermal regime of 10 °C [T = 10 °C], the maximum recorded longevity in wild populations reaches approximately 23 years [am = approximately 23 years], placing this species among the longer-lived members of its genus. Such an extended lifespan is consistent with a life-history strategy that delays reproduction and spreads reproductive effort across many seasons, a pattern often associated with deep-slope and seamount-associated fishes. The physiological mechanisms underlying this longevity are not yet fully understood, but the stable, cold temperatures of the species' preferred habitat likely contribute to reduced metabolic rates and slower cellular aging. Comparative data from related beryciform species suggest that this lifespan is near the upper end of the family range.

Populations of Beryx splendens are known to exhibit considerable variation in growth rates across their geographic range, which likely influences the size at which individuals become reproductively active. In regions where food availability is lower, fish may not surpass the size threshold for gonadal maturation of 33.2 centimeters [Lp = 33.2 centimeters] until several years later than their counterparts in more productive waters, potentially affecting the overall productivity of the stock. The maximum total length of 70 centimeters [Li = 70 centimeters] is seldom observed in heavily fished areas, where large individuals have been selectively removed over successive decades, a pattern consistent with documented growth overfishing in other seamount-associated beryciforms. Similarly, an adult body mass exceeding 4000 grams [Wwi = 4000 grams] has become a rare sight in many historical fishing grounds, underscoring the impact of sustained exploitation on the size structure of these populations. Effective management requires a thorough understanding of these life-history parameters to set appropriate catch limits that allow sufficient spawning biomass to persist.
